question:
A 62-year-old female patient with myelodysplastic syndrome who underwent bone marrow
transplantation from an unrelated donor shows persistent severe thrombocytopenia. Despite multiple
transfusions with apheresis platelets, her platelet count remains at 6000 per mm3 (normal range:

150,000–350,000). The patient has no fever, and laboratory tests show no evidence of disseminated
intravascular coagulation or thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Which of the following represents
the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Initiate intravenous
immunoglobulin therapy (B) Switch to pooled platelet transfusions (C) Initiate glucocorticoid therapy at
1 mg/kg of body weight (D) Begin plasmapheresis treatment (E) Observe the patient without initiating
further platelet transfusions (F) Perform bone marrow biopsy to assess engraftment (G) Test for
cytomegalovirus infection (H) Perform human leukocyte antigen antibody testing (I) Perform
platelet-specific antibody testing (J) Administer recombinant thrombopoietin
 A. Perform human leukocyte antigen antibody testing
B. Perform bone marrow biopsy to assess engraftment
C. Observe the patient without initiating further platelet transfusions
D. Initiate intravenous immunoglobulin therapy
E. Perform platelet-specific antibody testing
F. Initiate glucocorticoid therapy at 1 mg/kg of body weight
G. Switch to pooled platelet transfusions
H. Begin plasmapheresis treatment
I. Administer recombinant thrombopoietin
J. Test for cytomegalovirus infection
